title: Pea Princess seed
description: Part of Pea Princess (vet-flat) by Hsien Hao (Jacky) Chen - https://github.com/jacky18008/pea-princess - CC BY 4.0. The object behind a seed code: a person's rental preferences, reduced so that they can be posted in public. The code is the four characters PP1. followed by base64url of this object with no padding; scripts/seed.py writes and reads it, and references/seed-format.md tells a model how to do the same by hand. THE KEYS BELOW ARE THE WHOLE ALLOW-LIST. A seed never carries an address, a person's or a company's name, a workplace, an exact budget, an exact date, savings, income, an income-check route, a self-introduction, or anything about health, nationality, ethnicity, religion or immigration status. If you are writing a seed by hand and a value does not fit one of these keys, leave it out; do not invent a key. Empty values are omitted rather than sent as null.

v.description: Seed format version. 1 today. A reader that does not know the version must say so and stop, not guess.

n.description: A label the person chose for this seed, such as 'quiet, high, morning sun'. Their own name never goes here.

t.description: The kind of home, from profile.yaml `flat_type`.

b.description: The budget as a BAND, never as the person's real ceiling: for example '£2,000–2,400 all-in'. Round the ceiling up to the nearest 100 for the top of the band and take 200 off it below £1,500, otherwise 400. Exact numbers appear only when the person asked for them with --exact.

m.description: How deep this person runs the checks, from profile.yaml `budget_mode`.

c.description: Where they commute to, reduced to a postcode district ('WC2R'), a zone ('Zone 1') or a borough. Never a full postcode, an address, a campus, an office or an employer. Leave it out if you cannot reduce it.

w.description: The move-in window as a month, '2026-10'. Exact dates are never shared: they say when a stranger's flat is empty.

mh.description: Must-haves, in the person's own plain words.

av.description: Deal-breakers, in the person's own plain words.

pr.description: The top three priorities, in order: quiet, light, price, space, commute, and so on.

qs.description: The questions this person makes every report answer, in their own words. The most useful thing in a seed, and the part worth copying from someone else: an agent that imports this seed must answer each one by name. An entry is either a bare string, which means `when: vet, kind: answer`, or an object. `trigger` is never shared: it stays in the sender's profile.

oneOf.description: The question, at the defaults: asked while the flat is being checked, answered from data.

text.description: The question in the person's own words.

when.description: Which stage it belongs to. filter = before any work, it decides whether a flat is worth looking at; vet = while the flat is being checked (the default); compare = only once there is more than one candidate; viewing = on the day, in the flat; sign = just before the contract. Missing means vet.

kind.description: What answers it. answer = the agent works it out from data (the default); ask = it is put to the landlord or agent in writing; check = the person checks it themselves, with their own eyes, nose or ears. Missing means answer.

reject_ground_floor.description: true = a ground-floor flat is an automatic no.

reject_no_sky.description: true = windows that cannot see sky are an automatic no.

best_aspects.description: The compass directions they scored highest, not the whole score table.

q.description: true = quiet wins when quiet and light conflict.

fw.description: The plan for the first weeks after arriving. This is the only key allowed out of profile.yaml `bridging`; nothing else under it is shareable.

s.description: The three-sentence summary the agent wrote from the person's stories about places they have lived (profile.yaml `story_summary`). Derived preferences only: the stories themselves are never stored, quoted or shared. A long seed drops this key first to stay short enough to paste; the card still carries it.

journey.description: OPTIONAL and separate from the seed: journey.json, the running record of one person's search, kept next to profile.yaml. The agent appends one candidate per flat it vets. seed.py --journey turns it into the 'what I found' lines on the card: how many flats, how the verdicts fell, and what was chosen. Nothing in this file is written into a seed code.

started.description: The day the search started, as 2026-09-05.

profile_seed.description: The seed code this search started from, if it started from one.

candidates.description: One entry per flat vetted, appended as you go.

id.description: Your own short id for the flat, matching the report.

label.description: What the flat was, in words, WITH NO ADDRESS: '2019 build, courtyard side, 4th floor'. A label with a postcode in it is scrubbed before it reaches a card.

tier.description: The escalation tier that run used: standard or breadth.

chosen.description: The flat that was taken, if the search ended.

label.description: What it was, in words, with no address.

area_m2.description: Indoor area in square metres from the energy certificate.

all_in_band.description: What it costs all-in, as a band.

address.description: OPTIONAL and off by default. It is printed on a card only when the person passes --reveal-address. Leave it out unless you have a reason to keep it here.

notes.description: Whatever the person wants to remember. Never printed on a card.
